assessment.profile_description: Standard security assessment: passive set plus nmap web ports, exposed-file probes, gobuster, nikto and nuclei with safe settings.

authorization.statement: Operator confirmed ownership of, or written permission to test, the in-scope assets.

findings.title: CORS reflects arbitrary origin with credentials
findings.description: The server reflects an untrusted Origin and allows credentials, which can let malicious sites read authenticated responses.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: Origin: https://doxa-cors-test.invalid -> Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://doxa-cors-test.invalid; Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
findings.impact: A malicious website may be able to read responses from this application in a victim browser.
findings.remediation: Validate Origin against a strict allow-list; never reflect arbitrary origins with credentials.
findings.false_positive_notes: Impact depends on whether the endpoint returns sensitive, authenticated data.

findings.title: Exposed Git repository metadata
findings.description: The .git directory is downloadable, allowing source code and history to be reconstructed.

cvss.justification: Repository metadata was confirmed readable without authentication; full source retrieval was not attempted, so confidentiality impact is scored Low.

findings.evidence: GET /.git/HEAD -> HTTP 200; content signature matched. ref: refs/heads/main
findings.impact: Sensitive configuration, source code or data may be disclosed to unauthenticated users, enabling follow-on attacks.
findings.remediation: Remove the file from the web root, deny access in the web-server configuration and rotate any credentials it contained.
findings.false_positive_notes: Signature matched file content. Confirm manually that this is not an intentional public file or a honeypot.

findings.title: Exposed environment file (.env)
findings.description: The .env file is publicly readable and typically holds credentials and API keys.

cvss.justification: Readable configuration file whose variable names indicate credentials or keys (values redacted and not used).

findings.evidence:
GET /.env -> HTTP 200; content signature matched. DB_PASSWORD=<redacted>
APP_KEY=<redacted>
DEBUG=<redacted>
findings.impact: Sensitive configuration, source code or data may be disclosed to unauthenticated users, enabling follow-on attacks.
findings.remediation: Remove the file from the web root, deny access in the web-server configuration and rotate any credentials it contained.
findings.false_positive_notes: Signature matched file content. Confirm manually that this is not an intentional public file or a honeypot.

findings.title: Cookie without HttpOnly attribute
findings.description: Cookies without HttpOnly can be read by JavaScript and stolen through XSS.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: Cookie names (values not stored): sid
findings.impact: Session cookies may be exposed to script access or sent over insecure channels, increasing the risk of session theft.
findings.remediation: Set the HttpOnly attribute on cookies that JavaScript does not need.
findings.false_positive_notes: Cookies used only for client-side preferences may legitimately omit HttpOnly.

findings.title: Directory listing enabled
findings.description: The web server lists directory contents, exposing file names and potentially sensitive files.

cvss.justification: Directory index confirmed readable without authentication; sensitivity of the listed files was not assessed, so confidentiality impact is scored Low.

findings.evidence: GET /backup/ -> HTTP 200; auto-index page detected: Index of /backup/
findings.impact: Technical details help attackers choose and tune attacks against the system.
findings.remediation: Disable directory indexing (Options -Indexes, autoindex off) and review exposed files.
findings.false_positive_notes: Intentional public file mirrors may be listed on purpose.

findings.title: Site served only over unencrypted HTTP
findings.description: No HTTPS service was found; all traffic, including any credentials, is sent in cleartext.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.impact: Traffic may be intercepted or modified in transit, exposing credentials and user data.
findings.remediation: Deploy a valid TLS certificate, enable HTTPS and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
findings.false_positive_notes: Local lab targets commonly use plain HTTP.

findings.title: phpinfo() page exposed
findings.description: phpinfo output discloses configuration, paths and environment details.

cvss.justification: Configuration or runtime information confirmed readable without authentication.

findings.evidence: GET /phpinfo.php -> HTTP 200; content signature matched. <html><title>phpinfo()</title><body>PHP Version 5.6.40</body></html>
findings.impact: Sensitive configuration, source code or data may be disclosed to unauthenticated users, enabling follow-on attacks.
findings.remediation: Remove the file from the web root, deny access in the web-server configuration and rotate any credentials it contained.
findings.false_positive_notes: Signature matched file content. Confirm manually that this is not an intentional public file or a honeypot.

findings.title: Cookie without SameSite attribute
findings.description: Without SameSite, cookies are sent on cross-site requests in older browsers, aiding CSRF.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: Cookie names (values not stored): sid
findings.impact: Session cookies may be exposed to script access or sent over insecure channels, increasing the risk of session theft.
findings.remediation: Set SameSite=Lax or Strict (None only with Secure when required).
findings.false_positive_notes: Modern browsers default to Lax, reducing the practical risk.

findings.title: HTTP TRACE method enabled
findings.description: TRACE echoes requests back, which can aid cross-site tracing attacks.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: TRACE / -> HTTP 200 and the probe header was echoed
findings.impact: Weak configuration may expose unnecessary functionality or information.
findings.remediation: Disable TRACE (e.g. TraceEnable off).

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header
findings.description: No CSP is set, so the browser has no policy limiting where scripts and other resources may load from, reducing defence against XSS.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: LabServer/1.2.3 
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 22:32:42 GMT
Content-Type: text/html
Content-Length: 196
Connection: close
Set-Cookie: sid=<redacted>; Path=/
Set-Cookie: pref=<redacted>; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
X-Powered-By: PHP/5.6.40
findings.impact: Browsers are not instructed to apply defence-in-depth protections, which makes exploitation of other flaws (XSS, clickjacking, downgrade attacks) easier.
findings.remediation: Define a restrictive Content-Security-Policy (avoid unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval).
findings.false_positive_notes: Severity is context dependent; static or non-sensitive sites may accept this risk.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options header
findings.description: Without nosniff, browsers may MIME-sniff responses, enabling content-type confusion attacks.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.title: Missing clickjacking protection (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
findings.description: The page can be embedded in third-party frames, enabling clickjacking.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.title: Potentially dangerous HTTP methods advertised
findings.description: The Allow header lists state-changing methods. DOXA did not test them (would modify data).

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE
findings.impact: Weak configuration may expose unnecessary functionality or information.
findings.remediation: Disable unused HTTP methods and require authentication for write methods.
findings.false_positive_notes: Advertised methods may still require authentication.

findings.title: Version information disclosed in server header
findings.description: The server header discloses software and version details that help attackers select exploits.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: server: LabServer/1.2.3
findings.impact: Technical details help attackers choose and tune attacks against the system.
findings.remediation: Remove or genericise version banners (e.g. ServerTokens Prod, server_tokens off, expose_php=Off).
findings.false_positive_notes: Disclosure alone is not exploitable; it only reduces attacker effort.

findings.title: Version information disclosed in x-powered-by header
findings.description: The x-powered-by header discloses software and version details that help attackers select exploits.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: x-powered-by: PHP/5.6.40
findings.impact: Technical details help attackers choose and tune attacks against the system.
findings.remediation: Remove or genericise version banners (e.g. ServerTokens Prod, server_tokens off, expose_php=Off).
findings.false_positive_notes: Disclosure alone is not exploitable; it only reduces attacker effort.

findings.title: robots.txt references sensitive-looking paths
findings.description: robots.txt is public and lists paths that suggest administrative, backup or internal content, which helps attackers prioritise targets.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence:
Disallow: /admin/
Disallow: /backup/
findings.impact: Technical details help attackers choose and tune attacks against the system.
findings.remediation: Do not rely on robots.txt to hide content; protect sensitive paths with authentication and remove revealing entries.
findings.false_positive_notes: Paths may be harmless or decoys. Verify whether the listed resources are actually reachable.

limitations: Point-in-time, unauthenticated black-box assessment; authenticated areas, session handling after login and business logic were not tested.
Automated scanners produce false positives and false negatives; every finding classified as Potential or Unverified requires manual validation.
No exploitation, credential extraction, data modification, file upload, brute-force or denial-of-service testing was performed.
Only approved hosts and ports were contacted; redirects to unapproved destinations were not followed.
Wordlist-based discovery cannot prove absence of content; JavaScript-rendered routes and authenticated API endpoints were not enumerated.
OWASP Top 10 mapping is indicative. It does not establish compliance or non-compliance with any standard.
CVSS scores are provided only where the evidence supports a defensible vector; all other findings are intentionally not scored.
No screenshots were captured (no headless browser found).
